scope: Bounded survey of six additional views after target review. This is not exhaustive voxel-wise annotation or anatomical validation.

records.region: Earlier separated cut: right-sided chamber, trabecular and chordal structures
records.observation: The displayed chamber is open; branching and sheet-like structures remain connected to source-supported walls/leaflet regions. No additional separable object was established in this view.
records.decision: Retain; no new exclusion visible at this cut.

records.region: Mid-heart cut with great vessel, atrial rear surface and ventricular interior
records.observation: Bounded wall/fringe changes are visible. A small rough oval remains on the deeper-cut rear surface; this view does not by itself establish additional wrongly excluded wall support.
records.decision: Retain unresolved roughness; do not extend restoration beyond the two validated footprints.

records.region: Later great-vessel/atrial aspect and exterior-adjacent surface
records.observation: The known PA wall-adjacent arc remains visible. Other surface ridges and irregular transitions remain attached or unresolved at this view.
records.decision: Retain attached/ambiguous roughness; no additional blanket selection.

records.region: Apical myocardium and narrow endocardial spaces
records.observation: The cut reveals densely patterned myocardium with narrow channels and connected endocardial structures. No independently separable large object was established in this sampled view.
records.decision: Retain; exact same readback as v26 in this view.

records.observation: The epicardial surface retains small pits, ridges and surface irregularity. No new isolated target was established from this exterior view.
records.decision: Retain source-supported surface texture; no extra surface stripping.

records.observation: Corrected reversed plane normal exposes the opposite chamber/vessel surfaces. The bounded sheet selections are visible from the opposite side; wall, leaflet and branching structures remain.
records.decision: Retain remaining attached or unresolved structures; no additional free object established.
